post.description: Checks the email and password and starts a web session: the response sets the session cookie. A session the request already carries ends. A wrong address or password answers 401, always with the same message; a body that breaks the schema answers 400, 413, 415 or 422, and no error detail echoes a value it sent. After 10 failed sign-ins in 15 minutes from one address, or for one account, sign-ins from there or for it answer 429 with Retry-After until the 15 minutes have passed; sign-ins still being checked count too. When too many passwords are being checked at once, a sign-in that waited 10 seconds answers 503 with Retry-After.

schema.description: The session cookie: __Host-tdeemon_session over HTTPS (tdeemon_session over plain HTTP), HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, for the session's lifetime.

post.description: Ends the request's web session, if any, and clears the cookie. Signing out twice is fine.

post.description: Saves a food, or corrects one: the food with the id, or else the one of the same name and brand, keeping its id; else a new one. A save replaces the whole food: a field left out (a serving, an alias, an optional nutrient, the note) is cleared, so correct a food from what find_foods gave, without its last_use. archived archives the food, or keeps it so; left out, a save brings an archived food back. A name and brand, or an alias, another food has is refused (409), naming that food, which may be archived and so in no search: get_food gives it.

Each value belongs to the calendar date of its point; the merge keeps a manual value, the day's first weighing and the larger of a running total (DESIGN.md §4). The body is archived as it came; a user's days older than 30 go with their next body.

Strong's CSV export, the whole history, as the body or as the part file of a form: an API token with the ingest scope, not a web session. The day each workout starts in, by the user's day start hour, becomes a day with a workout, which makes it a training day unless the check-in's toggle says otherwise; the days of an earlier export that this one lacks are no longer. An export without a workout is refused. The body is archived as it came, and the latest export that read is kept for the training module.

post.description: Logs a meal under the client's UUIDv7 (201); the same meal sent again under it is a retry (200), another a conflict (409). An item is a food of the user's by its food_id, or a new food, which is saved, each with a quantity in the food's unit (g or ml), servings or portions; or an estimate of a whole plate. The answer holds the meal with what each item brought, where its day stands, and warnings: values that do not add up, or a meal that looks like one logged minutes before.

200.description: The same sent again: a retry.

delete.description: Deletes a meal, and says where its day stands without it. Its id stays the deleted meal's: a meal logged under it again is refused (409).

patch.description: Changes a meal: when it was eaten, its words, and its items, by ops in order: add an item, replace one, remove one. An item no op touches keeps what it brought when logged, though its food was corrected since. An add of an item the meal has under its id is a retry when it is the same, a conflict (409) when not; a remove of an item no longer there changes nothing.

get.description: Needs a web session. The tokens themselves are never shown again.

post.description: Needs a web session. The response carries the token, once. A device or a client then sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
